reason: A's gradient hero card and nested tiles are card soup, and its money in/out amounts wrap mid-number; at AX-XL A breaks badly. B is a restrained native list with daily subtotals and realistic merchants. B also truncates names at AX-XL, though less badly.

A is restrained, with one accent and a clean type ramp, and holds up at AX-XL. B breaks at AX-XL (price wraps, CTA truncated), shows the price twice and uses more color. A lacks back navigation, and its black swatch disappears in dark mode.

A has no monthly/yearly plan picker (misses the brief), uses gradient icons and colored tiles, and its CTA truncates at AX-XL. B has clear plan cards, a trial timeline, restore/terms and full renewal copy. B's flaws: timeline clipped under the footer and imbalanced plan cards.

A shows the monthly/yearly plans asked for, with selection, per-month math, a savings badge, a trial timeline and full price disclosure, in restrained serif-plus-one-accent styling. B has no plan picker, colored icon tiles, a gradient hero, a tiny close button and a truncated CTA at AX-XL.

A: one clear hero number, single orange accent, inset grouped run list. But a red '43% vs all of last week' mid-week reads as alarming, and at AX-XL text clips at the left edge. B: ring competes with the hero, gradient bars, four icon colours, card soup; at AX-XL B's ring breaks to '10…'.

B: one hero number with de-emphasized cents, a pace marker and a grouped native list. A: purple gradient hero, four-tile action row, colored-icon card grid; at AX-XL it wraps 'US$6 2/day', truncates labels and the Budgets header collides with the tab bar. B reflows cleanly, though its $/US$ labels are inconsistent and the tab bar overlaps content.

A: confident serif headline, sample note card with real content, one orange accent, holds at AX-XL ('Ask your notes' row clipped by the footer). B: template-like purple gradient, glowing mic competing with the headline; at AX-XL the CAPTURE label overlaps and body text is cut off.

A crams segmented tabs, a saved-account card, SSO, divider, inline form and a near-invisible disabled CTA into one screen. B: one headline and three thumb-zone buttons. Both break at AX-XL: B's headline clips and its Apple button doesn't scale; A's controls stay fixed while the email truncates. B uses a plain 'G' instead of Google's logo.

A: restrained, one headline, clear button ladder, inverted Apple button in dark mode; but a large dead gap, and at AX-XL the pinned footer clips the headline and drops the subtitle. B stacks too much, has a low-contrast disabled CTA, and its card truncates at AX-XL.

A breaks at AX-XL: the CAPTURE eyebrow overlaps, body copy is cut mid-sentence, page dots collide; it leans on a purple glow and gradient mic. B reflows with a pinned CTA, serif headline, one accent, specific transcript. B's light-mode scroll content is cut off awkwardly under the footer.

A: restrained native grouped list with daily totals, monochrome glyphs, green only for incoming money. B: gradient hero, colored icon tiles, money in/out amounts wrap mid-number at default size. Both break at AX-XL, B worse. A's dark mode is flat pure black.

A: one dominant number with de-emphasized cents, pace insight, single accent, reflows at AX-XL; inconsistent $ vs US$. B: glowing purple gradient card, quick-action grid, colorful icon tiles; breaks at AX-XL; low-contrast grey secondary text.

A ignores Dynamic Type (its AX-XL column matches default) and piles on rainbow icon tiles, a crown, an Active pill, a progress bar and blue toggles. B is restrained, icon-free, with reading-app-specific copy and helpful footers; rows stack at AX-XL. Flaws: truncated email, oddly indented value.

B: one large distance number, single accent, Swift Charts-style bars, named runs. A: card soup, gradient ring and bars, four colored icons. At AX-XL A truncates its ring, but B is worse: it loses side margins so 'DISTANCE' and the delta clip. B's red 'down 43%' mid-week reads as an alarm.

A breaks at AX-XL ('US$129./99', 'Add…', 'No size se…' cut) and overuses accent (red badges, orange stars, gray disabled CTA, repeated price). B is restrained and survives large text; it has no back button, a hero that is too large, and a black swatch that disappears in dark mode.

B ignores Dynamic Type. A reflows by stacking values under labels (middle-truncated email, small avatar); copy fits a reading app. B: generic toggles, crown emoji, icon on every row, a storage bar that doesn't belong; but its subscription card gives a clearer focal point.
